title: Craneport telecom low-latency integration notes
content:
Context:
- Customer: Craneport Telecom (regional carrier). POCs: Lena Park (SRE), Iris Nguyen (PM). Use-case: real-time call-routing assistant + short-form transcript summarization for operator dashboards. Goal: p95 latency <= 50ms for inference path for 128-token responses; sustained qps target 800 requests/sec during peak.

Call notes (2026-03-01):
- Quick intro: Craneport already runs k8s on a private cloud (OVH/Equinix). They prefer VPC Private deployment but are open to Dedicated in a partner region if latency is lower.
- Primary concern: jitter from mobile uplinks -> want fast tail latency and predictable p95.
- Data residency: EU regional, all audio/text must remain in their VPC. KMS integration mandatory (customer-managed keys).
- Feature asks: streaming partial responses to UI, function/tool calling to surface DB lookups, and embeddings for similarity search of prior tickets.
- Budget: initial pilot cushion ~ $12k/mo. Long-term committed spend TBD; price sensitivity on token count and caching effectiveness.

Technical requirements summary (customer stated):
- Deployment: Redwood Private (VPC) preferred, option to evaluate Dedicated pool in eu-west-1 for comparison.
- KMS: must support external HSM/KMS and allow key rotation without redeploying containers.
- Network: mutual TLS to Redwood control plane; local egress must be avoidable (strict air-gap constraints for some zones).
- Performance: p95 inference <= 50ms for 128-token outputs; cold-start p95 <= 250ms for 1s warm windows.
- Throughput: peak 800 rps sustained for 20min bursts, steady-state 200 rps.
- Model: customer wants open-model recommendation (no proprietary weights) — prefer Llama2-13B-8bit or similarly quantized 13B family with streaming enabled.
- Safety/QA: deterministic prompt tests + daily regressions from a prompt set of ~150 queries.

Operational gotchas we discussed:
- KV cache warm-up: Craneport expects sticky routing to keep KV cache hot for conversational flows. That conflicts with autoscaling and multi-az placement; need to define acceptable cache-warmth window and sticky-session policy.
- Sticky sessions and LB timeouts: Their LB currently times out idle TCP at 60s which causes streaming session drops. Recommend LB timeout >= 300s or use websocket keepalive.
- Small prompt variance -> batching risk: bursts of very small requests (10–20 tokens) will either need aggressive micro-batching or will blow p95 if we queue too long. Need to choose batching latency budget per route.
- Quantization compatibility: their custom tokenization for telco jargon produced long token sequences on tests; 8-bit quantization sometimes increases memory pressure for long sequences. Must run memory spike tests.
- Cold-starts with GPU assignment: dedicated GPU provisioning in private mode can cause 150–400ms cold-starts depending on model cache priming. We should test priming strategies (prefetch kv/vocab).
- Streaming + function-calls: when streaming is enabled and an incoming function call triggers external DB lookup, we need a plan to pause/resume streaming and not violate UI expectations.
- Network egress policy: some Craneport zones cannot call external control plane during strict maintenance windows. Need an offline bootstrap path for agent config changes.

Preliminary technical risks / hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: Using small-sequence-optimized kernels + prefix KV caching will achieve p95 <= 50ms at 200 rps but may struggle at 800 rps unless we reserve dedicated capacity.
- Hypothesis B: Sticky routing with a short session affinity (30s) will provide 60–70% cache-hit for conversation flows, significantly reducing token cost.
- Hypothesis C: On their k8s flavor, NVIDIA MIG not available; multi-tenant GPU sharing might not be feasible — likely need node-level isolation for predictability.

Requested artifacts / follow-ups from Craneport during pilot:
- Representative traffic trace (1 hour capture) with token length histogram and inter-arrival times (Dev/ops to provide by 2026-03-10).
- Example prompt/response pairs for core flows (50 examples).
- KMS policy contact + network egress whitelist IPs for test plane.

Immediate next steps (action items):
- (Maya) Prepare short config template for Redwood Private deploy tailored to Craneport (includes VPC peering options, control-plane egress exceptions, KMS steps). ETA 2026-03-05.
- (Devon) Run a local lab run on Llama2-13B-8bit with synthetic traces (two profiles: 200 rps steady, 800 rps 20min burst) and capture p95 tail for 128-token outputs. Deliver raw metrics + a short readme. ETA 2026-03-08.
- (Marco) Validate LB timeout recommendations and provide a minimal keepalive websocket snippet + kube service annotations to make sticky sessions robust. ETA 2026-03-06.
- (Lena @ Craneport) Share traffic trace and 50 sample prompts by 2026-03-10. Confirm KMS contact.
- Schedule deep tech call (2h) to run through priming strategy, canary plan, and network constraints. Proposed window: 2026-03-11 09:00–11:00 UTC. (Maya to send invite).

Decision points to resolve on tech call:
- Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private with reserved node pools: cost / SLA tradeoffs for peak 800 rps.
- Session affinity length (30s vs 120s) and cache-eviction policy for KV cache.
- Streaming behavior when function calls are synchronous vs async (UI handling).

Notes-to-self (observations / reminders):
- Put emphasis on demonstrating caching hit-rate -> biggest lever for token-cost savings.
- Prepare a short explainer on how quantization + kernel choices affect tail memory usage (customer nervous about OOMs).
- Bring a short list of similar telecom customers (anonymized) and their latency outcomes to build confidence.

Meeting log / quick timeline:
- 2026-03-01 initial intake call (phone).
- 2026-03-05 deliver private-deploy template (in flight).
- 2026-03-08 lab run metrics (Devon).
- 2026-03-11 deep tech call (pending scheduling confirmation).

Open questions for Craneport to answer before pilot sign-off:
- Can they accept a small outbound control-plane IP range for agent updates? If not, do they want an air-gapped bundle deployment path?
- Are there regulatory record-retention limits that affect logging granularity (we assume 90 days by default)?
- Preferred SLA targets for Dedicated vs Private (their procurement requires line items).

Raw action checklist (for our team):
- [ ] Draft Private deployment config (Maya).
- [ ] Lab-run Llama2-13B-8bit stress tests + memory profiles (Devon).
- [ ] Sticky-session guide + LB keepalive sample (Marco).
- [ ] Prepare quantization memory explainer + kernel selection doc (quick 2-page).
- [ ] Assemble anonymized telecom latency case studies (1 pager).

End of notes.
